source_evidence.observation: The paper distinguishes a dense matrix A from its BLR representation A_tilde, uses p by p blocks of size b by b with n = pb, leaves diagonal blocks uncompressed, specifies the two off-diagonal low-rank factor orientations, requires orthonormal columns in X_ij, chooses minimum admissible block ranks, defines local and global thresholds, and declares the analysis normwise in the Frobenius norm. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, Section 2.1 and eqs. (2.2)-(2.4)]

source_evidence.anchor: Frobenius-norm continuation, equation (2.5), and gamma definition
source_evidence.observation: The Frobenius norm is related to block norms by the square root of the sum of squared block norms. Floating-point operations satisfy fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u, and gamma_k = ku/(1-ku) for ku < 1; the stated gamma relations also permit noninteger indices. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, Frobenius-norm continuation and eq. (2.5)]

Computed truncated-SVD blocks satisfy A_tilde_ij = A_ij + Delta A_ij with ||Delta A_ij|| <= epsilon beta_ij, rounding errors in the compression are ignored, and the standing analysis assumes unit roundoff u safely smaller than epsilon. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1]

source_evidence.anchor: Opening of Section 4 and definition of r
source_evidence.observation: Section 4 defines r as the largest rank among off-diagonal blocks of the BLR LU factors; r can exceed the BLR rank of the input and is determined by the matrix and threshold rather than chosen independently. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, opening of Section 4]

Algorithm 1 is the UFC update-factor-compress trace. Theorem 4.1 assumes a nonsingular real matrix partitioned into p squared blocks of order b and requires Algorithm 1 to run to completion before asserting a computed BLR factorization bound. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 963, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1]

For UFC, the paper introduces scaled local and global compression parameters that remove diagonal-factor norms from the truncation bound; these yield xi_p = 1 and xi_p = p without intermediate recompressions. [PDF p. 17, printed p. 967, eqs. (4.13)-(4.15)]

Table 1 gives xi_p as 1, p, p, and p^2/sqrt(6) for, respectively, local without recompression, global without recompression, local with recompression, and global with recompression. Theorem 4.2 gives the UFC predecessor bound with c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1 and Theorem 4.2, eq. (4.16)]

Algorithm 2 is the UCF update-compress-factor trace. Theorem 4.3 assumes a nonsingular real matrix, a p squared block partition of order b, and successful completion, and supplies the same form of factorization predecessor bound with xi_p from Table 1. [PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Algorithm 2 and Theorem 4.3, eq. (4.17)]

Theorem 4.4 analyzes block triangular substitution for a triangular BLR matrix and gives (T_tilde + Delta T_tilde)x_hat = v + Delta v, with ||Delta T_tilde|| <= gamma_c||T_tilde|| and ||Delta v|| <= gamma_p||v||, where its local constant is c = b + r^(3/2) + p. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4 and eq. (4.21)]

Equation (4.22) records the blockwise lower-triangular execution. Theorem 4.5 explicitly binds A_tilde but then writes the system and conclusions using unadorned A; it states the perturbed equation and both norm bounds, with c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p and xi_p from Table 1. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.22) and Theorem 4.5, eqs. (4.23)-(4.25)]

The proof composes the factorization perturbation with perturbations from the two triangular solves by exact products, then bounds the final matrix perturbation using gamma_3c plus O(u epsilon) and the final right-hand-side perturbation using gamma_p plus O(u^2). [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, proof of Theorem 4.5]

binders: Theorem 4.5 explicitly binds A_tilde in R^(n by n), described as a pb by pb BLR matrix, and v in R^n. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 opening sentence]

The unadorned A occurring in Ax = v and equations (4.23)-(4.24) is not separately bound in Theorem 4.5; Section 2.1 defines A as the dense matrix represented by A_tilde. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eq. (2.2); PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 and eqs. (4.23)-(4.24)]
The inherited block parameters are p and b with p by p blocks, each of size b by b, and n = pb. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, discussion following eq. (2.3)]
epsilon > 0 is the LR threshold, u is the unit roundoff, and beta_ij specifies the scale of each compression error. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eq. (2.4); PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, eq. (2.5)]
r is the maximum off-diagonal rank in the computed BLR LU factors, not the input BLR rank. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, opening definition of r]

For each admissible input and successful permitted execution producing L_tilde, U_tilde, y_hat, and x_hat, the conclusion introduces final perturbations Delta A and Delta v after those computed quantities are fixed. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5, eqs. (4.23)-(4.25); PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, proof of Theorem 4.5]
hypotheses: Explicitly, the system Ax = v is solved by first solving L_tilde y = v and then U_tilde x = y, where L_tilde and U_tilde are BLR LU factors computed by either Algorithm 1 or Algorithm 2. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 opening sentence]

Inherited through Theorems 4.2 and 4.3, the underlying unadorned A is nonsingular and partitioned into p squared blocks of order b. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3]
Inherited through Theorems 4.2 and 4.3, the selected factorization algorithm must run to completion. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3]
Each off-diagonal compression obeys the truncated-SVD model A_tilde_ij = A_ij + Delta A_ij with ||Delta A_ij|| <= epsilon beta_ij. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1]
The standing analysis assumes u safely smaller than epsilon so that compression-rounding errors may be ignored relative to the prescribed truncation error. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1]

The triangular solves use the block-substitution operation analyzed in Theorem 4.4; for the displayed lower-triangular trace, x_i consists of entries (i-1)b+1 through ib and T_ii x_i is solved against v_i minus the sum over j = 1 through i-1. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4]

The gamma quantities used in the bounds are defined only in the regime ku < 1; in particular, the displayed gamma_p and gamma_3c require valid indices under that definition. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, gamma definition; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)]
A choice of local or global threshold and whether intermediate recompressions are performed determines xi_p through Table 1. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1]
conclusions: There are final perturbations Delta A and Delta v such that (A + Delta A)x_hat = v + Delta v. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.23)]
The coefficient-matrix perturbation satisfies ||Delta A|| <= (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| + gamma_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| + O(u epsilon). [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]
The right-hand-side perturbation satisfies ||Delta v|| <= gamma_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2). [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.25)]

Writing the proof's perturbations with distinct names, the exact matrix-side composition is Delta A_final = Delta A_factor + Delta L U_tilde + L_tilde Delta U + Delta L Delta U. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, first exact product in the proof of Theorem 4.5]

With the same disambiguating renaming, the exact right-hand-side composition is Delta v_final = Delta v_lower + L_tilde Delta y_hat + Delta L Delta y_hat. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, second exact product in the proof of Theorem 4.5]
definitions_and_conventions: A_tilde is defined in Section 2.1 as a BLR representation of a dense matrix A: diagonal blocks remain A_ii and off-diagonal blocks are replaced by low-rank approximations A_tilde_ij. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eq. (2.2)]
For i > j, A_tilde_ij = X_ij Y_ij^T; for i < j, A_tilde_ij = Y_ij X_ij^T. Both X_ij and Y_ij are b by k_ij, and X_ij has orthonormal columns. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eq. (2.3)]
The rank k_ij is the minimum ell_ij for which ||A_ij - A_tilde_ij|| <= epsilon beta_ij and rank(A_tilde_ij) = ell_ij. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eq. (2.4)]
The base local threshold uses beta_ij = ||A_ij||, while the base global threshold uses beta_ij = ||A||. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, discussion following eq. (2.4)]

For UFC, the later simplified bounds use scaled local parameters beta_ik = ||A_ik||/||U_tilde_kk|| for i > k and beta_ik = ||A_ik||/||L_tilde_ii|| for i < k, or the analogous global parameters with ||A|| in the numerator. [PDF p. 17, printed p. 967, eqs. (4.13)-(4.15)]
With intermediate recompressions, an additional update error H_ik is accumulated, and Table 1 incorporates its effect into xi_p. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Section 4.1.3 and Table 1]

A tilde denotes a BLR representation or BLR factor, while a hat denotes a computed solution or intermediate; in particular, L_tilde and U_tilde are computed BLR factors even though they are not written with hats. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 963, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]
implicit_context: All matrices and vectors in the theorem chain are real. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]

Nonsingularity and runs-to-completion are not restated in Theorem 4.5 but are inherited because its proof invokes Theorems 4.2 and 4.3. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, proof opening; PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3]

The block triangular solves must themselves complete with usable diagonal triangular blocks; Theorem 4.4's proof invokes the nonsingular triangular-solve model of Lemma 2.2. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, Lemma 2.2; PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4]

The final proof uses the larger factorization constant c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p for both triangular-solve perturbations, although Theorem 4.4 alone states the smaller b + r^(3/2) + p. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, eq. (4.21); PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5; PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, proof]
No bounded-growth condition on ||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| is imposed in the theorem; that factor remains explicit in both final bounds. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)]

The source's dense-A versus BLR-A_tilde notation must remain unresolved because Theorem 4.5 binds A_tilde but perturbs unadorned A. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eq. (2.2); PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]
statement.algorithm_linkage: Theorem 4.5 permits the computed factors from either Algorithm 1, whose left-looking order is update then factor then compress (UFC), or Algorithm 2, whose order is update then compress then factor (UCF). It then links those factorization traces to two block triangular substitutions through Theorem 4.4. Optional intermediate recompressions during factorization change xi_p according to Table 1. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 963, Algorithm 1; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Algorithm 2; PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5; PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1]
numerical_model: Scalar operations use fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u, for op in {+, -, multiplication, division}. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, eq. (2.5)]

gamma_k is ku/(1-ku) for ku < 1, with j gamma_k <= gamma_jk and gamma_j + gamma_k + gamma_j gamma_k <= gamma_(j+k); noninteger gamma indices are explicitly allowed. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, gamma definition following eq. (2.5)]
Compression is modeled by the norm bound ||Delta A_ij|| <= epsilon beta_ij, with rounding errors in the truncated SVD omitted under Assumption 2.1. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1]

The precision is abstracted by u rather than fixed to a particular IEEE format, and the standing theorem analysis assumes u safely smaller than epsilon. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, eq. (2.5); PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1]

At block row i, equation (4.22) represents the computed lower-triangular operation as the sum from j = 1 through i of (T_tilde_ij + Delta T_tilde_ij)x_hat_j equaling v_i componentwise perturbed by a vector bounded with gamma_p. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.22)]
error_notions: The result is a normwise backward-error statement with simultaneous perturbations to the coefficient matrix and right-hand side. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.23)-(4.25)]
It is not a coefficient-only backward error because Delta v is generally nonzero. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.23) and (4.25)]

The matrix perturbation is controlled by both a truncation-and-input term proportional to ||A|| and a floating-point term proportional to ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]
The right-hand-side perturbation depends on ||v|| and on ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||; it is not stated solely as a relative multiple of ||v||. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.25)]
The paper explicitly rejects a componentwise interpretation because low-rank approximation errors generally satisfy only normwise bounds. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, paragraph following eq. (2.4)]
norms: Every unsubscripted matrix norm in the analysis is the Frobenius norm ||A||_F = (sum over i,j of |a_ij|^2)^(1/2). [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, Frobenius-norm convention]
For a block partition, ||A|| is the square root of the sum of the squared Frobenius norms of the blocks. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, continuation of the Frobenius-norm convention]

The Frobenius norm is used as a submultiplicative norm and is invariant under left multiplication by a matrix with orthonormal columns. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, Frobenius-norm discussion; PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, continuation]

The same unsubscripted notation is used for vectors v, x_hat, and Delta v; for vectors this is the Euclidean/Frobenius vector norm, although Theorem 4.5 does not relabel it separately. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, global norm convention; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.25)]
constants_and_indexing: The scalar dimension is n = pb, arising from a p by p block partition with b by b blocks. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, discussion following eq. (2.3)]
The final theorem's constant is exactly c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, line following eq. (4.25)]
r is the maximum rank of an off-diagonal block in the BLR LU factors and can differ from the input BLR rank. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, definition of r]
The coefficient bound uses gamma_(3c), not 3 gamma_c, while the right-hand-side bound uses gamma_p. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)]
Without intermediate recompressions, xi_p = 1 for a local threshold and xi_p = p for a global threshold. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1]
With intermediate recompressions, xi_p = p for a local threshold and xi_p = p^2/sqrt(6) for a global threshold. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1]

The displayed lower-triangular block substitution indexes x_i as x((i-1)b+1 : ib) and uses predecessors j = 1 through i-1; equation (4.22) then sums j = 1 through i after including the diagonal solve. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.22)]
higher_order_terms: The matrix perturbation bound retains an unspecified O(u epsilon) term. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]
The right-hand-side perturbation bound retains an unspecified O(u^2) term. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.25)]

The exact factor-and-solve product contains the quadratic term Delta L Delta U before simplification into the final gamma_(3c) and higher-order expression. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, first exact perturbation product]
The exact right-hand-side composition contains the quadratic term Delta L Delta y_hat before simplification into O(u^2). [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, second exact perturbation product]
The theorem gives no explicit constants or dimension dependence for either big-O term, and no O(epsilon^2) term appears in equations (4.24)-(4.25). [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)]
exceptional_values: The factorization guarantees require nonsingularity and successful completion; nonsingularity alone is not used to erase the runs-to-completion requirement. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3]
The gamma definition excludes indices k for which ku >= 1, so the theorem's displayed gamma terms are meaningful only in their valid regime. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, gamma definition]
The standard relative-error model does not explicitly specify behavior for overflow, gradual underflow, NaNs, infinities, or other IEEE exceptional values. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, eq. (2.5)]
No nonzero assumption is stated for v; v is simply any vector in R^n. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 opening sentence]
The BLR definition permits zero-rank approximations for sufficiently small blocks under a global threshold. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, discussion following eq. (2.4)]

undebatable_constraints: The final perturbed equation is (A + Delta A)x_hat = v + Delta v. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.23)]
The exact parenthesization of the first matrix-error term is (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A||. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]
The matrix-error factor term is gamma_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde||, followed by O(u epsilon). [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]
The exact right-hand-side bound is gamma_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2). [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.25)]

The constant is c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p, with r taken from the off-diagonal ranks of the BLR LU factors. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, definition of r; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, line following eq. (4.25)]

The four xi_p values are exactly 1, p, p, and p^2/sqrt(6) in the Table 1 order local/no recompression, global/no recompression, local/recompression, global/recompression. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1]
The permitted factorization variants are Algorithm 1 UFC and Algorithm 2 UCF. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5; PDF p. 13, printed p. 963, Algorithm 1; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Algorithm 2]

Nonsingularity and runs-to-completion are inherited from the factorization theorems used in the proof. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, proof opening]
All displayed matrix bounds use the Frobenius norm and are normwise rather than componentwise. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, Frobenius and normwise conventions]
Compression obeys ||Delta A_ij|| <= epsilon beta_ij under the standing regime that u is safely smaller than epsilon. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1]
Neither O(u epsilon) nor O(u^2) may be silently dropped from the source statement. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)]

The literal source distinction between the bound variable A_tilde and the unadorned A in the system and conclusion must be preserved as an ambiguity. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eq. (2.2); PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]

ambiguities.issue: Theorem 4.5 binds A_tilde but writes Ax = v and perturbs unadorned A. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 and eqs. (4.23)-(4.24)]
ambiguities.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly defines A_tilde as a BLR representation of a dense A, whereas the theorem begins with A_tilde in R^(n by n) but immediately changes to unadorned A without an equality or fresh binder. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eq. (2.2); PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]

[PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eq. (2.2); PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]

ambiguities.evidence: Equations (4.16) and (4.17) write A = L_tilde U_tilde + Delta A, while the proof of Theorem 4.5 writes A + Delta A = L_tilde U_tilde. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, eq. (4.16); PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, eq. (4.17); PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, proof opening]

[PDF p. 17, printed p. 967, Section 4.1.1 and Corollary 4.1; PDF p. 22, printed p. 972, proof and discussion of Theorem 4.3]

contract_plain_english: For an admissible real block system whose BLR LU factors are successfully computed by UFC or UCF and whose block compressions obey the truncated-SVD threshold model with u safely below epsilon, two computed block triangular solves produce x_hat for which both the matrix and right-hand side can be perturbed to make the equation exact. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1; PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5] The exact source bounds are ||Delta A|| <= (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| + gamma_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| + O(u epsilon) and ||Delta v|| <= gamma_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2), with c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)] Here r is the maximum off-diagonal rank in the BLR factors, and xi_p is 1, p, p, or p^2/sqrt(6) according to the local/global and no-recompression/recompression cases in Table 1. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, definition of r; PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1] All matrix norms are Frobenius norms, the guarantee is normwise rather than componentwise, and the two big-O terms remain part of the result. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, norm convention; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)] The source literally binds A_tilde but writes and perturbs unadorned A, so their exact relationship at Theorem 4.5 must be recorded as unresolved rather than silently identified. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eq. (2.2); PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]
